name: Colonial Iberian Americas

description.short: Three centuries of Spanish building in the Americas, where Iberian plans met indigenous labour, adobe, and a continent of new conditions.
description.long:
Spanish colonial building in the Americas is a translation problem worked out at scale over three hundred years: European plan diagrams executed by indigenous craftsmen in local materials, under a Church that wanted magnificence and a Crown that would not pay for it.

What emerged — massive plain walls, courtyards, arcaded corridors, tile roofs, and ornament concentrated at the portal — is the direct ancestor of the American Southwest's regional architecture, and by way of Mission Revival and Spanish Colonial Revival, of a substantial fraction of everything built in California, Arizona, Texas, and Florida since 1915.

defining_characteristics: European plan diagrams executed in local material by local labour
Courtyard and arcaded corredor as the organizing spatial devices
Massive adobe or rubble walls, plain except at the portal
Low-pitched clay tile roofs and long horizontal parapets
A genuinely new regional language rather than a diluted European one
